title: Tensor-Hom comparison for a single two-term Koszul factor with arbitrary tail
statement: Let $C$ be a small category, $J$ a Grothendieck topology, $O$ a commutative ring sheaf, $b$ a global section and $U=O[0]$. Write $P_m=[O\xrightarrow{b^{m+1}}O]$ in degrees $0,1$ and $D_m=[O\xrightarrow{b^{m+1}}O]$ in degrees $-1,0$, using [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system] and [def-cbc-signed-koszul-completion-model]. There are chain isomorphisms $a_{m,K}:D_m\otimes\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m\otimes K,U)$ for every $m\in\mathbb N$ and arbitrary integer cochain complex $K$ of $O$-modules. These are contravariantly natural in $K$. The transition $(b,1):D_{m+1}\to D_m$ of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-negative-koszul-transitions] corresponds under these isomorphisms to precomposition by $(1,b)\otimes\mathrm{id}_K$ on $P_m\otimes K$. For any chain map $p:K\to U$, let $v_p:O\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,U)^0$ be inverse single-complex identification followed by inverse evaluation at one and precomposition by $p$. If $j_m:O\to D_m^0$ is the canonical rank-one basis inclusion, then the map $O\xrightarrow{\lambda_O^{-1}}O\otimes O\xrightarrow{j_m\otimes v_p}D_m^0\otimes\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,U)^0$ followed by the $(0,0)$ total-tensor inclusion and $a_{m,K}^0$ equals inverse single-complex identification followed by inverse evaluation at one and precomposition by $P_m\otimes K\xrightarrow{\pi_m\otimes p}U\otimes U\xrightarrow{\lambda_U}U$, where $\pi_m$ is the positive factor projection. There is no boundedness condition on $K$, no finite negative tensor of a list, and no derived-category or limit construction.

proof.text: Project Hom(L,O[0]) in degree n to its unique potentially nonzero coordinate, with source degree p satisfying p+n=0. All other factors have zero target; the product universal property constructs an inverse to this projection. Transport the remaining target term to O. Standard evaluation at one identifies the rank-one internal Homs with O. Normalize these rank-one identifications by the automorphism comparing their value on O[0] with the prescribed Hom-unit evaluation isomorphism. Endomorphisms of the monoidal unit commute (the unitor naturality and interchange identities prove this), so the normalized rank-one identifications still intertwine every scalar map. The Hom differential from -1 to 0 is positive precomposition by the positive differential. The two normalized rank-one identifications therefore give a chain isomorphism q_m:D_m -> Hom(P_m,O[0]); outside degrees -1 and 0 both sides are zero.

Compare q_m with the explicit factor transitions after projecting and applying the normalized rank-one identifications in degrees -1 and 0. Componentwise Hom functoriality changes (1,b) to (b,1), exactly the negative transition. The normalization was chosen so that projection and rank-one evaluation on Hom(O[0],O[0]) coincide with the prescribed Hom-unit evaluation. Consequently the degree-zero basis inclusion j_m:O[0] -> D_m is sent to inverse Hom-unit evaluation followed by precomposition with the positive projection pi_m:P_m -> O[0]. These chain maps agree on the supported degrees; all other source terms are zero.

In the ordinary closed structure on module-sheaf complexes, define the dual product [X,1] tensor [Y,1] -> [X tensor Y,1] by transposing the middle-four interchange followed by the two evaluations and the unit multiplication. Naturality follows by transposing and using evaluation naturality. This map factors as ihomUnitTensorToIhom X [Y,1], internal uncurrying, and precomposition with inverse braiding Y tensor X -> X tensor Y. The braided coherence and evaluation identities prove that factorization. The positive Koszul factor is dualizable by the existing bounded finite-Koszul theorem; hence all three maps are isomorphisms, for arbitrary Y=K. Transposing the two maps pi_m and p shows that the product of their transposes is the transpose of (pi_m tensor p) followed by unit multiplication.

Define e_m,K as q_m tensor identity followed by the dual product. Its naturality in K is the naturality of the dual product in its second source; compatibility with m uses the transition identity for q_m and naturality in its first source. For the normalized degree-zero equation, apply the dual-product transpose identity to pi_m and p, replace the transpose of pi_m by j_m followed by q_m, and use inverse Hom-unit evaluation for the transpose of p. Take degree zero and precompose with the inverse single-object identification. The component formula for the tensor left unitor and the tensor-inclusion naturality give precisely the displayed basis tensor. No invertibility of b, nonzero ring, boundedness of K, or nonempty site is used.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul: finite free dual identification. Z5 constructs the two supported degrees of the one-factor dual, normalizes rank-one evaluation by the prescribed Hom unit using commuting unit endomorphisms, and applies ordinary closed-category dualizability to obtain the tensor-Hom comparison, transitions, and degree-zero normalization.

theorem ringedNegativeKoszulFactorHomTensor
    (b : (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections) :
    ∃ e : ∀ (m : ℕ) (K : ringedSiteComplex O),
      ((ringedKoszulTensor O).obj (ringedNegativeKoszulFactor O b m)).obj
          (homComplex (R := O) K (ringedSiteRingComplex O)) ≅
        homComplex (R := O)
          (((ringedKoszulTensor O).obj (ringedKoszulFactor O b m)).obj K)
          (ringedSiteRingComplex O),
      (∀ (m : ℕ) (K K' : ringedSiteComplex O) (f : K' ⟶ K),
        ((ringedKoszulTensor O).obj (ringedNegativeKoszulFactor O b m)).map
            (((homComplexFunctor (R := O)).map f.op).app _) ≫ (e m K').hom =
          (e m K).hom ≫ ((homComplexFunctor (R := O)).map
            (((ringedKoszulTensor O).obj (ringedKoszulFactor O b m)).map f).op).app _) ∧
      (∀ (m : ℕ) (K : ringedSiteComplex O),
        ((ringedKoszulTensor O).map
            (ringedNegativeKoszulFactorTransition O b m)).app _ ≫ (e m K).hom =
          (e (m + 1) K).hom ≫ ((homComplexFunctor (R := O)).map
            (((ringedKoszulTensor O).map (ringedKoszulFactorStep O b m)).app K).op).app _) ∧
      (∀ (m : ℕ) (K : ringedSiteComplex O) (p : K ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex O),
        (MonoidalCategory.leftUnitor
            (SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))).inv ≫
          MonoidalCategory.tensorHom (ringedNegativeKoszulFactorBasis O b m 0)
            ((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 _).inv ≫
              (ringedHomUnitEvaluationIso O (ringedSiteRingComplex O)).inv.f 0 ≫
              (((homComplexFunctor (R := O)).map p.op).app _).f 0) ≫
          CochainComplex.ιMapBifunctor (ringedNegativeKoszulFactor O b m)
            (homComplex (R := O) K (ringedSiteRingComplex O))
            (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _) 0 0 0 (by omega) ≫ (e m K).hom.f 0 =
        (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 _).inv ≫
          (ringedHomUnitEvaluationIso O (ringedSiteRingComplex O)).inv.f 0 ≫
          (((homComplexFunctor (R := O)).map
            (((ringedKoszulTensor O).map (ringedKoszulFactorProjection O b m)).app K ≫
              ((ringedKoszulTensor O).obj (ringedSiteRingComplex O)).map p ≫
              (ringedKoszulUnitTensorIso O).hom).op).app _).f 0)
